deep.reconstruction: This page contains no mathematics. It is a printed Latin doctoral diploma (broadsheet) of the University of Göttingen in the Kingdom of Hanover. The heading names King George V of Hanover as Rector Magnificentissimus and Heinrich Albert Zachariä (jurist) as Prorector. In it the Dean of the medical faculty, Karl Friedrich Heinrich Marx (1796–1877), declares that Johann Robert Brandmann of Hamburg has been created Doctor of Medicine, Surgery and Obstetrics. This followed an examination and a public lecture 'de sectione caesarea post mortem' (on post-mortem caesarean section). The date is 14 March 1866 (MDCCCLXVI). The printer is the Dieterich academic press, Wilh. Fr. Kaestner. The seal is indicated only by 'L S' (locus sigilli) in a wreath. There are no handwritten annotations, formulas, computations or figures visible. The sheet was presumably among the printed academic announcements routinely circulated to Göttingen professors. Riemann was in Göttingen in early 1866, before leaving for Italy in June. It ended up in his papers, possibly kept as scrap paper; the verso may carry notes, but this side has none. There is nothing to reconstruct mathematically.

results.what: Printed Göttingen medical doctoral diploma for J. R. Brandmann, 14 March 1866; no mathematical content
